content:
The **fastest animal on land** is the **cheetah** (*Acinonyx jubatus*), which can reach speeds of **60 to 70 miles per hour (97 to 113 km/h)** in short bursts covering distances up to about 500 meters (1,640 feet).

However, if we consider **all environments**, the **fastest animal overall** is the **peregrine falcon** (*Falco peregrinus*). During its hunting dive (called a stoop), it can reach speeds exceeding **240 miles per hour (386 km/h)**—making it the fastest member of the animal kingdom.

So, to summarize:
- **Land**: Cheetah (~70 mph / 113 km/h)
- **Air (level flight)**: Common swift (~69 mph / 111 km/h)
- **Air (diving)**: Peregrine falcon (>240 mph / 386 km/h)
- **Water**: Black marlin or sailfish (estimates vary, but up to ~68 mph / 110 km/h)

The peregrine falcon holds the record for the **absolute fastest speed** achieved by any animal.
